correctness.rationale: The similarity characterization converts the radius into the infimum of matrix norm over scalar similarities. In a common upper-triangular basis, diagonal scaling suppresses all strict upper entries and yields the upper bound by Ruan's direct-sum axiom. A norming scalar functional on the Banach space is completely bounded with the same norm; after amplification, the resulting scalar upper-triangular matrix retains the selected diagonal value as an eigenvalue under every similarity, proving the reverse bound. Lie's theorem gives the solvable-Lie corollary.
risks: Finite-dimensional complex matrices only; the result does not address the minimal spectral radius.
